issues.legal_issue: An unsuccessful resolution applicant whose plan could otherwise have been approved by the Committee of Creditors is an aggrieved person entitled to appeal under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
Approval of a proposed combination by the Competition Commission of India must be obtained before the Committee of Creditors approves a resolution plan containing that combination.
The requirement of prior Competition Commission approval under the proviso to Section 31(4) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code is mandatory, not directory.

The timelines under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code and the Competition Act do not justify treating the prior-approval requirement as directory, and a resolution applicant may seek combination approval before submitting its resolution plan.
A resolution professional cannot relax the statutory requirement that Competition Commission approval precede the Committee of Creditors’ consideration and approval of a resolution plan.

A resolution plan containing a combination cannot be approved by the Committee of Creditors before the Competition Commission has scrutinised and approved the combination, including any modifications.

The Competition Commission must issue a show-cause notice under Section 29(1) of the Competition Act to both the acquirer and the target company in a proposed combination arising from insolvency proceedings.
The Competition Commission’s failure to issue a show-cause notice to the target company and to follow the applicable procedural safeguards vitiates its conditional approval of the combination.
A resolution applicant’s voluntary modification proposing divestment of the target company’s assets requires the target company’s participation and approval.
Material discrepancies in operational-capacity data relied upon for a conditional combination approval undermine that approval when they were not adequately examined.
An appellate court may defer to the Competition Commission’s expert assessment of competitive effects and underlying data absent sufficient grounds to re-examine its factual conclusions.

After receiving a response to a show-cause notice under Section 29(1) of the Competition Act, the Competition Commission may decide that no further investigation or report from the Director General is required.

The proviso to Section 31(4) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code requires combination approval before the Committee of Creditors’ approval of a resolution plan, rather than merely before the Adjudicating Authority’s approval.
